Support for the efficacy and safety of berotralstat in the proposed indication is primarily based on a single, 24-week multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in 120 adult and adolescent patients with type I or II HAE, Study BCX7353-302.

result.text: Met primary endpoint for both doses: estimated attack rate 1.65 (110 mg) and 1.31 (150 mg) vs 2.35 (placebo) per 28 days; rate reduction 30.0% (p=0.024) and 44.2% (p<0.001) relative to placebo.

indication.text: Prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older (original 2020 approval).

citations.quote: ORLADEYO™ is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.

target_moa.text: Berotralstat is an orally administered inhibitor of active plasma kallikrein; it decreases vascular permeability and edema by reducing bradykinin, which is produced when kallikrein cleaves high-molecular-weight kininogen.

citations.quote: Berotralstat is an orally administered inhibitor of active plasma kallikrein for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in patients 12 years of age and older.

Berotralstat decreases vascular permeability and edema in patients with HAE by reducing the blood level of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator. Berotralstat decreases the bradykinin level by inhibiting kallikrein, a plasma serine protease responsible for bradykinin production.

modality.text: Small molecule (orally administered plasma kallikrein inhibitor)

key_safety.text: Main safety signals were gastrointestinal-related adverse reactions and transaminase elevations. Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): abdominal pain (110 mg 10%, 150 mg 23%), vomiting (10%, 15%), diarrhea (10%, 15%), back pain (2%, 10%), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (10%, 5%); GI reactions were more frequent with 150 mg.

orphan_indication.text: Berotralstat was granted orphan (therapy) designation on November 1, 2017 for HAE, which is categorized as an orphan disease.

citations.quote: Berotralstat was granted orphan therapy designation on November 1, 2017, and fast-track designation on August 2, 2018.

Although the exact prevalence is unknown, HAE is estimated to affect 1 in 10,000 to 50,000 individuals worldwide (approximately 6,000 to 10,000 individuals in the United States) and is categorized as an orphan disease.
Berotralstat has been granted orphan drug designation and is exempt from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act.

summary.text: Original 505(b)(1) NDA submitted by BioCryst on December 3, 2019 and reviewed under Standard review; berotralstat had orphan drug designation (Nov 1, 2017) and fast-track designation (Aug 2, 2018) and was approved December 3, 2020 based on a single pivotal Phase 3 trial (Study 302). No accelerated approval, breakthrough, or priority review; no advisory committee.
